problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨4{e}^{-4t},\,5{e}^{5t}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(1,6)$ when $t=0,$ calculate the components of the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$r(t)=⟨\,-{e}^{-4t}+2\,,$
{{field-1}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨4{e}^{-4t},\,5{e}^{5t}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 4{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t,\,\int 5{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-4t}+{C}_{1},\,{e}^{5t}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨1,6⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨-{e}^{-4(0)}+{C}_{1},\,{e}^{5(0)}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,6⟩ & =⟨-1+{C}_{1},\,1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=2$ and ${C}_{2}=5.$ Therefore, the position vector is

$$
r(t)=⟨-{e}^{-4t}+2,\,{e}^{5t}+5⟩.
$$
